ctx.x: Well, now Norman Granz says, they also quote Norman Granz as saving, "Sure, I pulled Johnny and the others out of the band. I'd been very close to him ever since 1941 when "Jump For Joy" was in Los Angeles. I was doing my

first jam sessions out there. I used him on jam sessions and from time to time after the war I was in at Duke's band concerts. I felt Johnny was kept down in the band. I wanted to record him outside the Ellington context, and that's why he and the others came out. Harry Carney almost came too, but he was afraid to quit, and anyway, we didn't need him. Johnny's band had one big hit, it was 'Castle Rock', which was like a Louis Jordan thing with no singing. After a time Greer didn't want to travel so we used Sam…
So now according to him, he pulled you all out of the band.
